lines.text: Five a.m. at a frosty trailhead.
Jen pulled off her gloves to find the tiny button on her headlamp.
By the time it turned on, her fingers were numb, and the hike hadn't even started.
Here's the fix. Keep your gloves on.
A motion-sensor headlamp turns on and off with a wave of your hand.
Charge it the night before and pack a spare light on longer hikes.
Save this before your next early start.
